correctness.rationale: The QR range projector identity reduces residual squared Frobenius norm to d-k plus (kappa^2-1)/(1+kappa^(4q+2) gamma), with gamma the inverse-Gaussian-Gram quadratic form. Gaussian invariance and Schur complementation give gamma=U/V in distribution with independent chi-square degrees k,d-k. Integrating the resulting beta law yields the exact expectation; endpoint-integral asymptotics give explicit coefficients for k=1, k=2 and k>=3, including q=0 and q>=1. Hypotheses, rank boundaries, kappa=1, and d=2 were checked. 460 direct QR, integral, special-case and asymptotic test assertions passed in the current delivered package; proof rather than samples establishes infinite conclusions.

originality.rationale: The exactly specified one-spike squared-Frobenius distribution, its all-fixed-(d,k,q) beta integral, and all three sharp spike-asymptotic constants are not implied by the inspected general bounds or the prior qualitative two-dimensional spike example. Earlier range finding, Gaussian power iteration, the one-column obstruction and oversampled Frobenius inequalities are acknowledged as prior work. Similar exact beta formulas in less visible specialist work remain a real precedence risk, so this is a qualified same-model assessment, not a uniqueness certificate. The accessible prior work also contains a Gaussian trace-sketch one-column overlap distribution and its linear spike coefficient; those overlapping subfacts are excluded from any claim of independent novelty. Novelty is assessed for the unified matrix approximation result including the k=2 logarithm, the k>=3 exact constants and every q power rate.
residual_risks: Gaussian principal-angle and Wishart literature may contain an equivalent beta-prime computation under another name, outside the inspected source corpus.
Embedding-based mathematical-record search does not prove novelty or exhaust unpublished and specialist sources.
An inaccessible or unindexed part of a broad review might contain an equivalent exact one-spike expectation; no conflicting covering statement was discovered.
The theorem applies only to the stated single-spike family and fixed-parameter asymptotic, not to arbitrary matrices.

A separately derived one-column beta-overlap factor and leading coefficient already exists in Gaussian trace-sketch analysis; the independent substantive contribution must be the combined k>=2 critical width and q-power regime theorem, not that isolated base subcase.

value.rationale: The concrete optimization question is how sketch width and subspace-power filtering interact when a single singular direction dominates a matrix. The transition in expected squared Frobenius excess from linear blow-up (one Gaussian column) through logarithmic blow-up (two) to boundedness (three or more) reflects sharp inverse-Wishart integrability, and the exact power-dependent rates reveal how additional matrix passes control the rare-miss tail. The result is a natural all-fixed-dimension benchmark, not an arbitrary numerical slice or already-tabulated parameter, and no general matrix-wide theorem is asserted.
